_strings.@@39e03fe2b50c: Empire State Child Credit — Full-year New York State resident with at least one qualifying child - your child, sibling, stepsibling or a descendant of any of them (including a stepchild, eligible foster child, adopted child, or a child placed with you for adoption) who is under 17 years old on December 31, 2025, lived with you more than half the year, did not provide over half of their own support, has not filed a joint return (except to claim a refund of withholding or estimated tax), and is a U.S. citizen/national or holds an ITIN issued by the IRS.

_strings.@@48f46cfcc8f1: Treaty conformity — NY conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from NY income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the NY return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: NY Form IT-201 begins from the federal return's income items (line 1 = "wages, salaries, tips, etc." from federal Form 1040 line 1z) and arrives at federal adjusted gross income on line 19. Because the return starts from federal AGI, income that is exempt from federal tax under a U.S. income tax treaty is already excluded from federal AGI and flows through to NY. NY's additions to federal AGI (IT-201 lines 20-23, with "other additions" detailed on Form IT-225) do not include any modification that adds back treaty-exempt income. The 2025 IT-225-I addition-modification chart (60 A-1xx plus 59 A-2xx codes) contains no code referencing a federal tax treaty, treaty-exempt wages/income, or nonresident-alien treaty exclusions (the word "treaty" appears ZERO times in the 2025 IT-225-I, re-counted this session). Net effect: starts from federal AGI and has no treaty addback, so treaty-exempt income is NOT re-taxed -> conforms = true. (Unlike CA, which adds treaty-exempt income back on Schedule CA, NY has no analogous addback.)

_strings.@@6c05018f5bc3: Real Property Tax Credit (circuit-breaker, homeowners and renters) — New York State resident for all of 2025 who occupied the same NY residence for at least six months, was not claimed as a dependent on another taxpayer's federal return, and whose residence was not completely exempted from real property taxes. Homeowners: did not own real property with a current market value of more than $85,000 during 2025 and paid real property taxes. Renters: average monthly rent (2025 IT-214 line 13) of $450 or less (the form takes 75% of rent when the rent includes charges for heat, gas, electricity, and furnishings).

_strings.@@8a3111dc9f24: Law change NOT modeled by the engine (status final_form_published): NEW FOR 2025 — the Empire State child credit is DECOUPLED from the federal child tax credit. The 33%-of-the-federal-credit (computed under the rules in effect for tax year 2017, before Public Law 115-97) / $100-per-child computation used through 2024 no longer applies. The credit now equals $1,000 per qualifying child under four years old plus $330 per qualifying child at least four but less than 17 years old, reduced by $16.50 for every $1,000 (federal AGI rounded DOWN to the nearest $1,000 on Form IT-213 line 6) by which federal AGI exceeds the filing-status threshold — $110,000 married filing joint, $75,000 single / head of household / qualifying surviving spouse, $55,000 married filing a separate return. If the computed Form IT-213 line 9 amount is zero or less the taxpayer is not eligible and must not complete or submit the form. Resolve via: 2025 Instructions for Form IT-213 (IT-213-I), "New for 2025" and "Credit Calculation" at the citation URL — the per-child amounts, the $16.50-per-$1,000 phase-down and the line 6 round-down rule live there; the credit reduces tax on IT-201 line 63 and is never a base reduction, so calc.state_tax does not compute it.

states.reason: Worked in NY in 2025 without living there — file a nonresident return on NY-source income.
warnings: Remote-work trap: work performed from TX for an employer sitting in NY, and NY HAS a convenience-of-the-employer sourcing rule. 20 NYCRR 132.18(a): a nonresident employee who works both in and out of New York allocates wages by working days, BUT "any allowance claimed for days worked outside New York State must be based upon the performance of services which of necessity, as distinguished from convenience, obligate the employee to out-of-state duties in the service of his employer" (the convenience of the employer test). A normal work day spent at an out-of-state home office therefore counts as a NEW YORK day (New York-source wages) unless the home office qualifies as a bona fide employer office. Trigger: Applies to a nonresident or part-year resident whose ASSIGNED OR PRIMARY work location is an established office or other bona fide place of business of the employer IN New York State. If the assigned or primary work location is outside New York, a normal work day worked at home is treated as a day worked OUTSIDE New York (TSB-M-06(5)I). Exceptions: TSB-M-06(5)I (tax years 2006+): a home-office day counts as worked outside New York only if the home office is a "bona fide employer office" — met by the PRIMARY factor (the home office contains or is near specialized facilities that cannot be made available at the employer's place of business) OR at least 4 of the 6 secondary factors (home office is a requirement or condition of employment; bona fide employer business purpose for the location; some core duties performed there; regular and continuous client/customer meetings there; no designated office space at the employer's regular place of business; employer reimburses substantially all (80%+) home-office expenses) AND 3 of the 10 other factors. The same rules apply to the Yonkers nonresident earnings tax. [TSB-M-06(5)I (NYS Dept. of Taxation and Finance, 2006-05-15), "New York Tax Treatment of Nonresidents and Part-Year Residents — Application of the Convenience of the Employer Test to Telecommuters and Others", quoting 20 NYCRR 132.18(a) and setting the primary / secondary / other bona-fide-employer-office factor test. — https://www.tax.ny.gov/pdf/memos/income/m06_5i.pdf] If the rule reaches these wages, a NONRESIDENT NY return is required that the physical footprint alone never shows.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: 2025 Form IT-201, page 3: '39 NYS tax on line 38 amount'. IT-201-I (2025) p. 12, Line 39 – New York State tax: 'Is line 33 (your New York adjusted gross income) $107,650 or less? If Yes, find your New York State tax using the 2025 New York State Tax Table (visit www.tax.ny.gov and search: table); or if line 38 is $65,000 or more, use the New York State tax rate schedule below. Enter the tax due on line 39. If No, see Tax computation – New York adjusted gross income of more than $107,650 below.' This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply Form IT-201, line 33 (New York adjusted gross income) = federal AGI (line 19) + New York additions (lines 20-23) - New York subtractions (lines 25-32). The op then subtracts the shipped NY standard deduction (form line 34) and $1,000 per dependent (form line 36) to reproduce NY taxable income (lines 37/38 = line 33 - line 34 - line 36), the amount the rate schedule is applied to. Do NOT supply federal AGI unless you have no NY modifications; do NOT supply line 38 (taxable income) or the deduction/exemption would be subtracted twice. Adjudication note (two-pass, TY2025): the schedules, standard deduction table, and $1,000 dependent exemption were drafted from the printer-friendly 2025 IT-201-I PDF (pp. 11, 33-39; InDesign build dated 2025-11-20) and re-verified against the separately published 2025 IT-201-I HTML edition plus the 2025 Form IT-201 fill-in PDF — all passes agree on every bound, rate, and printed constant. New York again did NOT index for 2025: all nine brackets, all printed constants, and the 8,000/16,050/8,000/11,200 standard deduction are unchanged from 2024 and 2023 (the mid-bracket bounds 8,500/11,700/13,900/80,650/215,400/1,077,550/5,000,000/25,000,000 for single/MFS, 17,150/23,600/27,900/161,550/323,200/2,155,350 for MFJ, and 12,800/17,650/20,900/107,650/269,300/1,616,450 for head of household were re-checked digit by digit against the 2025 print, not carried forward). CRITICAL — benefit-recapture worksheet mandate: if New York adjusted gross income (IT-201 line 33) is more than $107,650, the 2025 IT-201-I instructions MANDATE the 'Tax computation — New York adjusted gross income of more than $107,650' worksheets (pp. 34-39), so plain bracket math is WRONG (it understates tax) above that threshold; the filed form must use the worksheets. The 2025 Recapture Base / Incremental Benefit constants were RE-DERIVED from the 2025 booklet (not carried from 2024) and are: married filing jointly / qualifying surviving spouse — worksheet 1 (5.5% of line 38, stop if line 33 is $157,650 or more), worksheet 2 $333/$807, worksheet 3 $1,140/$2,747, worksheet 4 $3,887/$60,350, worksheet 5 $64,237/$32,500, worksheet 6 flat 10.9% of line 1; single and married filing separately — worksheet 7 (6% of line 38), worksheet 8 $568/$1,831, worksheet 9 $2,399/$30,172, worksheet 10 $32,571/$32,500, worksheet 11 flat 10.9%; head of household — worksheet 12, worksheet 13 $787/$2,289, worksheet 14 $3,076/$45,261, worksheet 15 $48,337/$32,500, worksheet 16 flat 10.9%. Each recapture is phased in over $50,000 of NYAGI above the bracket threshold (line 7 = lesser of the excess or $50,000, divided by $50,000 to four decimals). At NYAGI over $25,000,000 the final worksheet in each status taxes ALL taxable income at a flat 10.9%. Table mandate below $65,000: if NYAGI (line 33) is $107,650 or less and taxable income (line 38) is less than $65,000, the 2025 instructions require the 2025 New York State Tax Table (visit www.tax.ny.gov and search: table) — bracket math may differ by a few dollars within a table band; the filed form must use the table. The rate schedule itself applies only when line 38 is $65,000 or more (2025 IT-201-I p. 32 method table). One schedule covers Single AND Married filing separately ('Single and married filing separately—filing status 1 and 3') — the identical schedule is duplicated for both statuses here, copied, not derived. The MFJ schedule is titled 'Married filing jointly and qualifying surviving spouse—filing status 2 and 5', so qualifying surviving spouse maps exactly to married_filing_jointly as the engine assumes, and the 2025 standard deduction table lists qualifying surviving spouse at the same $16,050 as a married filing joint return. The printed '$X plus Y% of the excess over $Z' constants in the 2025 schedule are rounded to whole dollars and do NOT all equal the exact cumulative sum of prior brackets: max divergence is $0.50 (single/MFS $600 printed vs $599.50 exact at $13,900) and roughly plus or minus $0.25 elsewhere (e.g., MFJ $976 vs $976.25 at $23,600 and $8,553 vs $8,552.75 at $161,550; single top constants $449,929/$2,509,929 vs exact $449,929.45/$2,509,929.45; HoH $107,651 vs $107,650.90 and $434,163/$2,494,163 vs exact $434,163.475/$2,494,163.475) — the identical divergence pattern to the 2024 and 2023 prints. Pure marginal accumulation (what this engine does) can therefore differ from schedule arithmetic by under $1. Standard-deduction gates NOT modeled: a Single filer who CAN be claimed as a dependent on another taxpayer's return (item C = Yes) gets $3,100, not the shipped $8,000 (2025 standard deduction table, first row); married-filing-separately spouses must both take the standard deduction unless both choose to itemize on their New York returns; itemizers enter the larger Form IT-196 line 49 amount on line 34 instead. Compute those cases on the form. New York has no personal (taxpayer/spouse) exemption — only the $1,000 per-dependent exemption on line 36. If line 36 is more than line 35, the 2025 form says to leave lines 37 and 38 blank (taxable income zero) — the engine's max(0, ...) floor matches. Line 35 itself is already floored at zero ('if line 34 is more than line 33, enter 0'). New York State household credit (IT-201 line 40 — table 1 up to $75 for single, tables 2/3 by household size, no credit above federal AGI of $28,000/$32,000), NY EITC (line 65, 30% of the federal EIC), the Empire State child credit (line 63 — DECOUPLED from the federal child tax credit for 2025: $1,000 per qualifying child under four, $330 per child age four to 16, less $16.50 per $1,000 of federal AGI over $110,000/$75,000/$55,000), and the child/dependent care credit (line 64) are TAX CREDITS subtracted from tax, not base reductions — none are shipped as exemptions and none are modeled by this op. Local taxes on the same return are NOT modeled: New York City resident tax (separate NYC tax table / NYC tax rate schedule on p. 40 with its own worksheets), the NYC school tax credit (line 69) and NYC child and dependent care credit, the Yonkers resident income tax surcharge (a percentage of net state tax) and Yonkers nonresident earnings tax, and the MCTMT for self-employed individuals. New York STATE tax on line 39 only is modeled here. Whole-dollar entry is MANDATORY on the 2025 return ('enter whole dollar amounts only... Do not enter any cent amounts'), and the printed rounding rule is drop under 50 cents / increase 50 cents or more to the next dollar — a .50 tie rounds UP, exactly matching this op's irs_round. 2025 filing-season schedule confirmed final: New York had no mid-year 2025 rate change; these are the schedules printed in the final 2025 IT-201-I (printer-friendly PDF and HTML editions agree) used for the 2026 filing season.
